\section{The audit surface, measured}\label{sec:gen-surface}

Three measurements, one per part of the built code: the spine (what the two master theorems unfold to), Layer 1 (what becomes trusted when the adaptor and the executable verifier are built), and the public-input phase. Each is followed by the dossier's proposals to reduce it: what each removes, what it costs, and whether any statement changes.

The two dossiers count differently, and their line counts are not to be added: the spine's dossier counts a definition's lines from its head to the end of its data body without proof fields, and never a theorem's proof; the Layer 1 dossier counts a theorem up to \texttt{:=} and a definition in full. The public-input phase's dossier gives no line count; its catalogue's classes are tallied in the last subsection.

\subsubsection{Method (dossier section B.1)}\label{sec:gen-spine-B1}

\enquote{Load-bearing} is taken literally: a declaration is counted when the \textbf{statement} of a master theorem mentions it or unfolds to it, transitively, down to library objects. Three sets:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{C}: what \texttt{piop\_\allowbreak{}perfectCompleteness} unfolds to (\texttt{Compose.\allowbreak{}lean:162-{}164}): \texttt{Phases}, \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Complete} (so \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Def}, \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Complete}, \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}Def}, \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}Complete}), \texttt{leanVmPiop} (so \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}toDef}, \texttt{Def.\allowbreak{}append}, \texttt{commitDef}, the send-oracle reduction), \texttt{M3Rel} (so \texttt{M3Holds} and everything under it), the six seams (so every claim and its \texttt{Holds}), \texttt{TheOracle} and the evaluation oracle.
\item \textbf{Kx}: what \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} adds (\texttt{:181-{}184}): \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Security}, \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Security}, \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}Security}, \texttt{leanVmVerifier}, \texttt{piopError}.
\item \textbf{K}: what \texttt{piop\_\allowbreak{}rbrKnowledgeSoundness} adds by naming its extractor and state function (\texttt{:172-{}176}, \texttt{S.\allowbreak{}toDef.\allowbreak{}witMid}, \texttt{piopExtractor P S}, \texttt{S.\allowbreak{}toDef.\allowbreak{}kSF init impl}): the composition of securities (\texttt{Security.\allowbreak{}append}, \texttt{Complete.\allowbreak{}append} for its \texttt{guarded}, \texttt{guardedAppend}, \texttt{stateFunctionOfEq}), the ported state-function append (\texttt{KnowledgeAppend.\allowbreak{}state}, \texttt{left}, \texttt{right}, \texttt{Witness}, the two witness lemmas, \texttt{appendGuarded}) and the commit phase's security (\texttt{commitSecurity}, \texttt{commitComplete}, \texttt{commitExtractor}, \texttt{sendOracleSecurity}, \texttt{sendOracleComplete}, \texttt{sendVerifierPure}, \texttt{sendExtractor}, \texttt{sendWitMid}, \texttt{sendStateFunction}, \texttt{sendOracle\_\allowbreak{}relOut}).
\end{itemize}

Counting rule: a declaration's lines from its head to the end of its data body, excluding blank lines, comment-only lines and, for definitions, proof fields (\texttt{complete}, \texttt{rbr}, \texttt{toFun\_\allowbreak{}empty/\allowbreak{}next/\allowbreak{}full}, \texttt{verify\_\allowbreak{}eq}, …); \enquote{with docstrings} adds the docstring block above it and the field docstrings inside it. Proof bodies of theorems are never counted. The script is \texttt{probes/\allowbreak{}code-{}spine/\allowbreak{}surface.\allowbreak{}py}, which reads every file with \texttt{git show b435631:} and finds each declaration by name; its output is reproduced below. Structures' field docstrings are counted as docstrings, so \texttt{M3Instance} is 14 lines of code and 31 with its docstrings.

In words. To read \textbf{what perfect completeness says}, an auditor reads 70 declarations, 217 lines of Lean (382 with their docstrings): 75 in \texttt{Instance.\allowbreak{}lean} (the instance and the relation), 55 in \texttt{Seams.\allowbreak{}lean} (claims and seams), 25 in \texttt{Compose.\allowbreak{}lean}, 23 in \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}lean}, 18 in \texttt{SendOracle.\allowbreak{}lean} (the commit reduction), 13 in \texttt{Field.\allowbreak{}lean}, 6 in \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}lean}, 2 in \texttt{Oracles.\allowbreak{}lean}. \textbf{Knowledge soundness in its existential form} adds 6 declarations and 31 lines (the \texttt{Security} structures, the verifier, the error). \textbf{Knowledge soundness for the named extractor} adds 24 declarations and 106 lines, of which 38 are the ported state-function append and 25 the commit phase's security data. The whole \texttt{With} form is 100 declarations, 354 lines, 612 with docstrings.

\subsubsection{Proposals to reduce it (dossier section B.3)}\label{sec:gen-spine-B3}

Each: what is removed, what it costs, whether any statement changes. Lines are code lines of B.2.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{State the master knowledge theorem in the existential form and keep the named form as a lemma.} Removes from the reading list the 24 declarations of class K (106 lines): the composition of securities, the ported append, the commit phase's data. Costs: the named extractor leaves the theorem's statement; acceptance test 24 then rests on the lemma \texttt{piop\_\allowbreak{}rbrKnowledgeSoundness} (kept) and on \texttt{piopExtractedStack\_\allowbreak{}eq} (section F). Changes no statement; it changes which one is called the master theorem. Not recommended if the named extractor is what the base theorem (T4) must carry through Fiat–Shamir; recommended as the \emph{reading order} (the existential theorem first, the named one as its refinement).
\item \textbf{Delete \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e}} (2 lines, plus one line in every phase and in \texttt{Complete.\allowbreak{}append}): derivable for every component (D.7, ArkLib's \texttt{Prover.\allowbreak{}instOutputIsPureEmpty} at the pin). Costs one import (\texttt{NoAmbient}) or a four-line restatement. Changes no statement: \texttt{Complete} loses a field every instance discharges by \texttt{rfl}.
\item \textbf{Merge \texttt{TableOut} and \texttt{PubOut}} (4 lines, two structures that are both \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} L\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} I\allowbreak{})}; \texttt{FlockOut} is \texttt{TableOut} plus \texttt{weighted}). Replace by one \texttt{Pool I} with \texttt{columns} and \texttt{weighted}, and let each seam say which list is empty where it must be (\texttt{Seam.\allowbreak{}table}: \texttt{weighted = []}). Costs: the statement types of three phases become the same, so a phase in the wrong slot is caught by its seam proof, not by its type; the docstrings' \enquote{column claims, now with the public words' claims} become a comment on the seam. Changes the statements of \texttt{Seam.\allowbreak{}table}, \texttt{Seam.\allowbreak{}pub} (one conjunct each) and the fields of \texttt{Phases}. Recommended only if the sibling dossier's \texttt{BusOut} redesign is adopted, so that the statement types are revisited once.
\item \textbf{Derive \texttt{Layout.\allowbreak{}read} from \texttt{extend}} (C.2; \texttt{read} and \texttt{read\_\allowbreak{}eval} are 6 of \texttt{Layout}'s 6 lines, replaced by one law on \texttt{extend}). Costs: a lemma \enquote{the extension at a cube point is the entry} (CompPoly has it as \texttt{eval\_\allowbreak{}mle\_\allowbreak{}eq\_\allowbreak{}eval}, cited in \texttt{Field.\allowbreak{}lean:50}) and, for the toy, \texttt{slice} becomes a theorem. Changes the definition of \texttt{column} and hence of every clause, definitionally: no statement's meaning changes.
\item \textbf{Fold \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Def/\allowbreak{}Complete/\allowbreak{}Security}} (10 lines): three abbreviations of \texttt{Component.\allowbreak{}*} at \texttt{TheOracle I} and \texttt{Unit}; \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}passThrough*} likewise. A phase author writes \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} I\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} I\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} U\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} …} once. Costs: longer signatures in \texttt{Phases} (five fields). Changes no statement. Marginal; the abbreviations are the documented interface and cost 13 lines with docstrings.
\item \textbf{Drop \texttt{Weight.\allowbreak{}mle} and \texttt{mle\_\allowbreak{}eq}} (2 of \texttt{Weight}'s 4 lines): the seam never uses \texttt{mle} (\texttt{WeightedClaim.\allowbreak{}Holds} is \texttt{Weight.\allowbreak{}pair}, the cube sum). \texttt{mle} is the verifier's evaluator for the opening phase, a property of the \emph{phase}, not of the claim's truth. Costs: the opening phase must carry the evaluator itself (as a field of its \texttt{Def}, or by requiring \texttt{Weight} to be \texttt{MLE-{}friendly} there). Changes the statement of \texttt{Seam.\allowbreak{}flock} by removing a field nobody reads there. Recommended: it also removes the temptation to prove the seam by \texttt{mle} rather than by the cube sum.
\item \textbf{\texttt{M3Instance.\allowbreak{}d} with its two proof fields} (3 lines) could be replaced by a subtype of polynomials on \texttt{constraints} and \texttt{flushes} (section F, the degree finding): the two proof fields go, \texttt{Seam.\allowbreak{}bus} loses a conjunct, the table verifier loses a guard. Changes the statements of \texttt{M3Instance} and \texttt{Seam.\allowbreak{}bus}, and of \texttt{VirtualTerm}.
\item \textbf{Drop \texttt{decAux}} from \texttt{M3Instance} (2 lines with the attribute): decidability of \texttt{aux} is used by nothing load-bearing; the \texttt{Decidable} instances for \texttt{M3Holds} serve the tests. Costs: the tests declare \texttt{i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{} D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}x} locally. Changes the statement of \texttt{M3Instance}. Weak: an instance that cannot decide its own \texttt{aux} is a smell, and the read-everything phase (D.3 (d)) needs it; keep unless the field list is revisited.
\item \textbf{The \texttt{\{σ\} init impl} binders} (eleven declarations): forced by ArkLib (C.6). A wrapper \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Complete\textquotesingle{}} at \texttt{σ := Unit} would not compose (ArkLib's append needs every \texttt{s : σ}). Not removable at this pin.
\item \textbf{\texttt{sendOracle\_\allowbreak{}relOut}} (3 lines) is \texttt{Seam.\allowbreak{}commit} under another name, needed because the generic send-oracle component is stated for any relation; \texttt{commitComplete}'s type ascription is what makes the two coincide. Keep; note in \texttt{Compose.\allowbreak{}lean} that the coincidence is definitional, so an auditor need not read \texttt{sendOracle\_\allowbreak{}relOut}.
\item \textbf{\texttt{sendStateFunction}'s data is in the statement} (5 lines) only through the named form (K). If proposal 1 is taken it leaves the surface.
\end{enumerate}

What is \textbf{not} proposed: removing \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Complete} in favour of \texttt{Phases.\allowbreak{}Security} (\texttt{Security extends Complete}, and completeness is landed before security per convention \emph{Holes}); removing \texttt{p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s} (it is the smaller statement).

Net effect of proposals 2, 4, 6 and 7, all of which keep the theorems' meaning: about 15 code lines and two proof obligations per phase (\texttt{outputPure}, the degree of its terms) off the surface, and one guard out of the table phase's verifier.

\textbf{What an auditor must read, and when.}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Today: nothing.} The master theorems, the seams and the phase interfaces are stated over an abstract \texttt{I : M3Instance} and import no Layer 1 module (\texttt{Spine/\allowbreak{}Instance.\allowbreak{}lean} imports \texttt{Field}, \texttt{ToArkLib/\allowbreak{}Oracles} and CompPoly; \texttt{Seams.\allowbreak{}lean} imports \texttt{Instance}). The one built phase that touches Layer 1, the public-input phase, imports \texttt{ToCompPoly/\allowbreak{}Multilinear} privately (\texttt{PublicInput.\allowbreak{}lean:14}, \texttt{import}, not \texttt{public import}) and uses \texttt{boolVec\_\allowbreak{}zero}, \texttt{evalMle\_\allowbreak{}append\_\allowbreak{}boolVec}, \texttt{eval₂Mle\_\allowbreak{}cast} and \texttt{cubeIndex} inside one proof (\texttt{eval₂Mle\_\allowbreak{}linePoint}, \texttt{:71-{}89}); its definitions unfold none of them. Layer 1 is proved code whose statements nobody trusts yet.
\item \textbf{Once the adaptor is built} (\texttt{leanIsaInstance} with \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} :\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} (\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} h\allowbreak{}μ\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{} f\allowbreak{} h} and the index and bytecode columns as \texttt{Coord.\allowbreak{}known}): seventeen definitions, 61 lines (83 with docstrings): \texttt{Blocks}, \texttt{offsetNat}, \texttt{offset}, \texttt{total}, \texttt{selector}, \texttt{extendPoint}, \texttt{unstack}, \texttt{slice}, \texttt{cubeIndex}, \texttt{boolVec}, \texttt{cubeSplit}, \texttt{Layout.\allowbreak{}comap}, \texttt{readColumn}, \texttt{layout}, \texttt{powersTable}, \texttt{idxColumn}, \texttt{bytecodeColumn} (plus \texttt{encodeSlots}, \texttt{entry}, \texttt{derefFlags} and \texttt{Opcode.\allowbreak{}code} from the arithmetization and parameters), and the strided reader that does not exist yet (B.8).
\item \textbf{Once the executable verifier is built}: the evaluators it runs, \texttt{eqWeight} (its \texttt{mle}), \texttt{idxColumnEval}, \texttt{bytecodeColumnEval}, and, if the verifier computes \texttt{eq(\allowbreak{}sel\_\allowbreak{}b,\allowbreak{} ζ\_\allowbreak{}hi)} with Layer 1's function rather than its own, \texttt{selectorWeight}, \texttt{lowPoint}, \texttt{highPoint}, \texttt{lowVec}, \texttt{highVec}: eight definitions, 22 lines. The theorems relating them to the oracle (\texttt{idxColumn\_\allowbreak{}eval}, \texttt{bytecodeColumn\_\allowbreak{}eval}, \texttt{evalMle\_\allowbreak{}padHigh}, \texttt{stack\_\allowbreak{}eval\_\allowbreak{}ambient\_\allowbreak{}one}, \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}) are proved, so they are read for their statements only by whoever checks that the phases use them as intended.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Proposals to reduce it} (each with its saving in public declarations / statement lines):

\begin{enumerate}
\item Delete \texttt{BlockClaims.\allowbreak{}lean} and \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n} (8 / 30; 122 + 108 file lines). No module uses \texttt{BlockClaim}; the opening phase uses \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}, over an abstract instance, which the earlier review introduced for that reason; \texttt{isValid\_\allowbreak{}iff\_\allowbreak{}pairing} restates \texttt{unstack\_\allowbreak{}eval₂\_\allowbreak{}eq\_\allowbreak{}sumCube}; the locality lemmas have no consumer. Drop \texttt{BlockClaim} from the interface list (\texttt{protocol-{}blueprint.\allowbreak{}md:1404}). If the leanth credit matters, the derived-source notice can move with \texttt{unstack\_\allowbreak{}eval₂\_\allowbreak{}eq\_\allowbreak{}sumCube}.
\item Delete \texttt{bytecodeColumn\_\allowbreak{}slot} (1 / 2) and its three \texttt{example}s; point acceptance test 14 at \texttt{b\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c} and the oracle \texttt{\#guard}s (G.4). \texttt{bytecodeSlotColumn} and \texttt{slice\_\allowbreak{}bytecodeColumn} (2 / 4) have no consumer either; keep them only if the bus phase takes the per-slot form (\texttt{ValuesProbe}'s \texttt{bytecodeColumn\_\allowbreak{}answer\_\allowbreak{}slots}, which the earlier review recorded as open).
\item Remove the in-layer duplicates (\texttt{DuplicatesProbe}): \texttt{unstack\_\allowbreak{}eval} (a special case of \texttt{unstack\_\allowbreak{}eval₂}), \texttt{stack\_\allowbreak{}eval\_\allowbreak{}ambient\_\allowbreak{}zero}, \texttt{stackColumn\_\allowbreak{}eval} (no consumer), \texttt{stackColumn\_\allowbreak{}eval\_\allowbreak{}ambient} (honest stack only, no consumer): 4 / 14.
\item \texttt{prodVars}, \texttt{sumCube\_\allowbreak{}prodVars}, \texttt{evalMle\_\allowbreak{}prodVars} (3 / 5) prove nothing any other declaration uses; \texttt{sumCube\_\allowbreak{}padHigh} is the statement the table sumcheck needs. Either delete them and cite \texttt{sumCube\_\allowbreak{}padHigh} in acceptance test 7, or keep one as the specification's sentence.
\item Replace \texttt{evalMle\_\allowbreak{}lagrangeBasis} by CompPoly's \texttt{eqTilde\_\allowbreak{}eq\_\allowbreak{}prod} (1 / 2), or upstream the reordering; keep \texttt{eqWeight.\allowbreak{}mle} as it is.
\item The 66 helpers of the four \texttt{ToCompPoly} files are the upstream pull request's content, not audit surface; marking the ones used only inside their own file \texttt{private} (for example \texttt{cubeIndex\_\allowbreak{}div}, \texttt{cubeIndex\_\allowbreak{}mod}, \texttt{lowVec\_\allowbreak{}append}, \texttt{highVec\_\allowbreak{}append}, \texttt{slice\_\allowbreak{}placeSlice}, \texttt{windowTable*}, \texttt{stackAt\_\allowbreak{}decomposition}, \texttt{offsetNat\_\allowbreak{}succ}, \texttt{offsetNat\_\allowbreak{}mono}) would make the public list of each file read as its interface.
\end{enumerate}

Together 1 to 5 remove about 20 public declarations and 60 statement lines, and no load-bearing definition. The load-bearing core (20 definitions, 71 lines) is already small; the one addition it needs is the strided reader.

The dossier's remarks on the surface are two. First, on the flag \texttt{PublicLine.\allowbreak{}sent} (section E): 

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Does it enlarge what an auditor must trust?} By one Boolean per line, whose only effect in the phase as built is on the \emph{transcript's format} (which values are sent and checked): the pool does not depend on it beyond which claims carry a sent value, and with \texttt{pooled} reading the statement, not even that. In the deployed design (values sent pooled) \texttt{sent} decides which pooled values are prover-chosen, so it enters the soundness argument (the unsent lines' claims are at verifier-computed values, and their falsity is a bad challenge on its own). Either way the auditor's obligation is the same: \enquote{leanISA's instance sends exactly the two low limbs}, a transcript fact checked against the Rust (\texttt{:616-{}618}, \texttt{:747-{}749}).
\end{quote}

Second, the phase as merged is the result of a compression of the audit surface made by the earlier review (its item on a single output, \texttt{pooled}), and that compression removed the dependence of every theorem of the phase on the check of the prover's message; the dossier's finding on it is in the findings (the check on the public-input message is not load-bearing), with its evidence:

\begin{quote}
\emph{Evidence.} C.3 (the verifier with no check has \texttt{Phase.\allowbreak{}Security} at the same error, no \texttt{sorryAx}), C.4 (for every message function and every check the message passes, \texttt{securityG}; instances with no check, with forty-two zeros, with the swapped check and a matching prover), C.5 (the first-value check; the words' equation). Root cause: \texttt{pooled} (\texttt{PublicInput.\allowbreak{}lean:127-{}128}) reads the statement, not the message; the message enters \texttt{check} and nowhere else; the proof of \texttt{rbr} (\texttt{:350-{}366}) never mentions \texttt{check}. The build the earlier review read pooled the values sent, and its item \enquote{H1: one output, \texttt{pooled}} (\texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}-{}\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}3}) removed the dependence, so the same review's table \enquote{each of five wrong verifiers breaks a stated theorem} (\texttt{:104-{}114}, rows (i) and (v)) stopped being true of the code as merged; the status repeats the claim (\texttt{protocol-{}status.\allowbreak{}md:440}).
\end{quote}
